answer: Every review names a reviewer, a repository, and a date. Code review history counts that trail: a thousand reviewed pull requests on record. The trail is public and mirrored, so the lagoon of the idea is the record itself - a thousand small acts of judgement no forger can backfill. One fake needs a thousand plausible reviews; a hundred need a hundred thousand, and the walnut in the middle of each is a maintainer who must be fooled in person, in public. The timber that ends the story is the merge button: no merge, no record, no account.
